source_text: Vide qua imperitia reprehendere audeas eos qui contra mendacium pro veritate nituntur. Quis enim justius indignari contra alterum debuit? utrumne qui hostes Dei asserit, an vero qui adversus eum qui hostes Dei asserit pro Ecclesiae veritate consentit? Nisi quod imperitos etiam animosos atque iracundos esse manifestum est, dum per inopiam consilii et sermonis ad iracundiam facile vertuntur, ut de nullo alio magis quam de te dicat Scriptura divina: Homo animosus parat lites, et vir iracundus exaggerat peccata. Lites enim et dissensiones quantas parasti per Ecclesias totius mundi? Peccatum vero quam magnum tibi exaggerasti, quando te a tot gregibus scidisti! Excidisti enim te ipsum. Noli te fallere; siquidem ille est vere schismaticus qui se a communione ecclesiasticae unitatis apostatam fecerit: dum enim putas omnes a te abstineri posse, solum te ab omnibus abstinuisti. Nec te informare ad regulam veritatis et pacis vel Apostoli praecepta potuerunt monentis et dicentis: Obsecro ergo vos ego vinctus in Domino, digne ambulare vocatione qua vocati estis, cum omni humilitate sensus et lenitate, cum patientia sustinentes invicem in dilectione, satis agentes servare unitatem spiritus in conjunctione pacis; unum corpus, et unus spiritus, sicut vocati estis in una spe vocationis vestrae. Unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma, unus Deus et pater omnium, qui super omnes, et per omnia, et in omnibus nobis.
pass_a_gloss: See with what rashness you dare to reprehend those who strive for truth against falsehood. For who ought to be more justly indignant against another? Whether he who asserts that they are enemies of God, or truly he who consents to the truth of the Church against him who asserts that they are enemies of God? Except that it is clear that the rash are also spirited and irascible, while through lack of counsel and speech they easily turn to irascibility, so that divine Scripture says about no one more than about you: A spirited man prepares lawsuits, and an irascible man exaggerates sins. For how many lawsuits and dissensions have you prepared throughout the Churches of the whole world? How great a sin have you exaggerated for yourself, when you cut yourself off from so many flocks? For you have cast yourself out. Do not deceive yourself; for he is truly a schismatic who has made himself an apostate from the communion of ecclesiastical unity: while you think that all can be kept away from you, you alone have kept yourself away from all. Nor could the Apostle's precepts, warning and saying, instruct you according to the rule of truth and peace: I therefore beseech you, I, a prisoner in the Lord, to walk worthily of the vocation with which you have been called, with all humility of mind and gentleness, with patience bearing with one another in love, taking care to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace; one body, and one Spirit, as you have been called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in all of us.

rejected: to walk in a worthy manner

choices.why: conveying a soft and mild quality

bible_refs.note: Scripture quote about unity and peace

pass_b_english: Consider the rashness with which you dare to rebuke those who strive for the truth against falsehood. For who should more justly be indignant against another: the one who claims they are enemies of God, or the one who stands for the truth of the Church against the one who makes that claim? Unless it is simply that the rash are clearly also spirited and irascible, easily turning to anger through lack of counsel and speech, so that divine Scripture says of no one more than of you: "A spirited man prepares lawsuits, and an irascible man exaggerates sins" (Prov 17:19 LXX; cf. Prov 29:22). For how many lawsuits and dissensions have you stirred up throughout the churches of the whole world? How great a sin have you heaped upon yourself by cutting yourself off from so many flocks? You have cast yourself out. Do not deceive yourself; for the true schismatic is the one who makes himself an apostate from the communion of ecclesiastical unity: while you think that everyone else can be kept away from you, you alone have kept yourself away from everyone. Nor could the Apostle's precepts, warning and saying, instruct you according to the rule of truth and peace: "I therefore, a prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk worthy of the calling with which you have been called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace; one body and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all" (Eph 4:1–6).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent translation that correctly identifies the scriptural allusions (Proverbs 17:19 and Ephesians 4:1-6) which were present in the Latin text as implicit quotes. The title 'Condemning Schism' accurately reflects the thought of the passage.
